## Natural history notes

A small hairstreak butterfly characterized by gray-brown wings, thin white-edged lines, orange spots near the hindwing margin, and tiny tail-like extensions that can draw attention away from the head. In Florida, it is widespread in gardens, fields, roadsides, dunes, scrub, pine flatwoods, parks, and other sunny open habitats with flowers and low host plants. Adults visit many kinds of nectar plants, while the caterpillars feed on flowers, buds, fruits, and tender growth of a wide range of plants, including legumes, mallows, and many garden or weedy species.
